Indian Standard
SPECIFICATION FOR VEGETABLE TANNED LEATHER FOR BELTING

( First Revision)
0. FOREWORD

0.1 This Indian Standard ( First Revision ) was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 6 January 1978, after the draft finalized by the Leather Sectional Committee had been approved by the Chemical Division Council. 0.2 Leather beltings are used for driving machines in various industries. They are made from vegetable tanned heavy leather. 0.3 This standard was first published in 1964 and is now being revised in the light of the latest developments in the trade and technology. In this revision, values for total ash, solvent extractable substances, water soluble matter, hide substance and degree of tannage have been modified. These text methods for assessing the chemical requirements have now been referred to IS : 582-1970* and the text methods for physical requirements have been referred to IS : 5914-1970t. Regarding sampling and criteria for conformity, reference has been made to IS : 5868-1969:. 0.4 The Central Leather Research Institute, Madras supplied valuable data in the preparation of the standard. 0.5 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS : 2-19608. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value shouId be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.
*Methods tMethods $Methods �Rules for of chemical testing of leathers (jrgt r&en of physical testing of leather. of sampling for leather. rounding off numerical values ( wuire~ ). ).

3

IS : 2954 - 1978 1. SCOPE 1.1 This standard prescribes the requirements and the methods of sampling and test for vegetable tanned leather used for flat and round leather beltings. 2. TERMINOLOGY 2.1 For the purpose of this standard, given in IS : 1640-1960* shall apply. the following definitions and those

2.1.1 Temporary Elongation -The difference between the length of the stretched specimen and its initial length, expressed as a percentage of the original length. 2.1.2 Permanent Elongation - The residual increase in length of the test piece expressed as a percentage of the original length after subjecting it to a specified stress for a specified period. 3. REQUIREMENTS 3.1 Raw Material - The material shall be good quality wet-salted or green slaughtered buffalo, ox or COW hides of good substance. They shall be particularly free from defects, such as flay cuts, putrefaction and warble holes. butts shall be tanned with vegetable tanning 3.2 Tanning -The materials or synthetic tanning materials or a mixture of the two. Mineral acids shall not be used for plumping the hides either in pretanning stage or during tanning. A cut section of the leather made by knife shall be smooth showing that the inside fibre is compact and fully tanned. 3.3 gcouring and Washing-The tanned butts shall be scoured and washed on the grain and flesh sides neatly and may be skived or shaved on the flesh side to remove all traces of loose fibre. 3.4 StufEng - The stuffing materials shall be fish oil, tallow, or other oils, fats or waxes of suitable quality. 3.5 Oiling - The tanned leather shall be oiled with animal or vegetable oil of suitable quality. 3.6 Setting - During the currying process, the butts shall be uniformly well set out so as to minimize stretch and to give a smooth finish to the grain ( hair ) side. the stuffing process is complete, the 3.7 Seasoning ( Ageing ) -After butts shall be laid down to season for a minimum period of eight weeks.
*Glossary of

termsrelating to hides, akina and leather. 4

IS :2954 - 1978
,3.8 Stretching -The leather after stuffing may be set out and/or stretched to remove the stretch and the stretcher marks, if any, be cut off. 3.8.1 The stretching shall be from neck to butt along the backbone line. The damp butts shall be dried in the stretched condition. 3.9 Finishing - The strap butts or bends shall be finished on the grain and flesh sides and the thin protective layer of grease left during the period of seasoning shall be removed. In doing so, no damage shall be done to the leather surface. The grain side shall not be dope finished, but light staining is permissible. 3.10 Chemical Requirements -The leather shall comply with the chemical requirements given in Table 1 when tested in accordance with the methods referred to in co1 4.

NOTE-The use of the IS1 Certification Mark is governed by the provisions of the Indian Standards Institution ( Certification Marks ) Act and the Rules and Regulations The IS1 Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys made thereunder. the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well-defined system of inspection, testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by IS1 and operated by the producer. IS1 marked products are also continuously checked by IS1 for conformity to that standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions under which a liience for the use of the IS1 Certification Mark may be granted to manufacturers or processors, may be obtained from the Indian Standards Institution.
